Based on my review, the PR removes the email-assignment lines from `update_user` while keeping the `@require_auth` decorator and `is_owner_or_admin` check intact. The endpoint still returns `user.to_dict(include_email=True)` (line 53), but this is unchanged code that already existed in the base snapshot. The removed lines were the only user-controlled write path to `user.email`, and their removal does not introduce any new authorization weakness — the remaining code path is strictly narrower than before.

The policy (security-policy.md §2) states "A user may read or update ONLY their own profile" and the endpoint enforces this via `is_owner_or_admin`. The PR does not weaken this check. The api-spec.md documents PUT /users/<id> as "owner or admin" — the endpoint still matches that access rule; it simply no longer accepts an email field, which is a functional change, not an authorization flaw.

No CWE-639, CWE-862, or CWE-863 candidate flaw is introduced by this change.
